## Recommendation

**Decision:** Port the platform to direct Rust bindings for Apple frameworks, with AppKit owning the macOS shell and the existing Vexel UI remaining custom drawn. Keep AppKit types behind `platform/` interfaces. This fits the owner’s macOS 13+, custom UI, and no shipped first-party C/Objective-C requirements.

**Facts, checked 14 Oct 2026:** The objc2 project provides Rust bindings to Apple frameworks. Its published AppKit, Core Graphics, Core Text, and Metal crates are each at **0.3.2**, released **4 Oct 2025**. They use `Zlib OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT`; objc2’s core crate uses MIT. The project notes that its bindings derive from Apple SDKs and flags Xcode license terms as an area of uncertainty, so record that caveat for dependency review. The Metal crate’s published lockfile pairs 0.3.2 with `objc2 0.6.2`. [objc2 project and license](https://github.com/madsmtm/objc2), [AppKit 0.3.2](https://docs.rs/crate/objc2-app-kit/0.3.2), [Core Graphics 0.3.2](https://docs.rs/crate/objc2-core-graphics/0.3.2), [Core Text 0.3.2](https://docs.rs/crate/objc2-core-text/0.3.2), [Metal 0.3.2 and package lockfile](https://docs.rs/crate/objc2-metal/0.3.2).

**Inference / dependency proposal:** Start with `objc2`, `objc2-foundation`, `objc2-app-kit`, `objc2-core-graphics`, `objc2-core-text`, `objc2-metal`, and QuartzCore bindings for `CAMetalLayer`; enable only needed API features. Add `block2` for Objective-C completion blocks where required. Add `dispatch2` only if the design needs explicit GCD dispatch. Pin the compatible published versions and resolved transitive graph in a reviewed ADR/lockfile; the 0.6.2 pairing is evidence, not a claim that it is the newest objc2 release. Apple frameworks are OS dependencies, not vendored UI code. Review each API’s macOS availability against the 13.0 deployment target.

## UI choice

**Native bindings vs egui:** egui is MIT OR Apache-2.0, immediate-mode, custom paintable, and has optional AccessKit accessibility. It can produce a custom appearance, so it is not inherently incompatible with the visual lock. However, adopting it would replace Vexel’s retained widget/state/layout and pixel-painter modules, while AppKit integration would still be needed for shell, dialogs, menus, clipboard, and Metal. **Inference:** Direct bindings are the narrower migration path and better preserve the existing custom UI architecture. [egui repository, current manifest and license](https://github.com/emilk/egui).

## Scope and seams

Cover `src/platform/macos/` (window/events, menus, dialogs/files, clipboard, accessibility, Metal, text/localization, recovery and task queue); `src/ui/` (core, widgets, drawing, icons and viewer controls); and `src/app/` viewer runtime, events, rendering, chrome, editor, timeline and accessibility modules. The local READMEs and platform headers document current behavior and contracts.

Retain the platform seam as owned Rust types: opaque window/resource handles, bounded UTF-8 and byte buffers, explicit event/action enums, and owned event payloads. Keep application/editor models independent of AppKit classes. Match existing semantics for point-space input versus backing-pixel surfaces, scale-change events, key/modifier translation, file-open/drop paths, asynchronous open/save completion, command-state menus, native dialogs, bounded SVG/PNG clipboard formats, Core Text measurement/drawing, and VoiceOver names, values, actions, frames and change notifications. Apple documents that AppKit UI work belongs on the main thread; keep view/window/menu/dialog/clipboard/accessibility operations there and move parsing/raster/recovery work off-thread. [AppKit threading guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/uikit-appkit), [NSApplication event loop](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplication), [NSPasteboard](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nspasteboard), [NSAccessibilityProtocol](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsaccessibilityprotocol).

## Ownership, sequence, and risks

Keep `unsafe` inside a small platform FFI layer: document each pointer’s lifetime, retain/autorelease transition, callback/block capture, thread affinity and teardown order. Prefer objc2 retained handles and Rust-owned snapshots. Never let a callback outlive its window/app context; cancel or invalidate callbacks before releasing handles. `objc2` exposes retained Objective-C objects, but safe wrappers do not remove the need to uphold API invariants. [objc2 `Retained`](https://docs.rs/objc2/latest/objc2/rc/struct.Retained.html).

**Ready work-order sequence:** (1) freeze platform Rust types, FFI/thread/ownership rules and deployment target; (2) port AppKit startup, window, input/event queue and teardown; (3) dialogs, file open/drop, menus, clipboard and command routing; (4) Core Text, appearance and accessibility parity; (5) Metal device/layer/pipeline/presentation and bounded verification; (6) Rust UI primitives and viewer/chrome/editor integration; (7) native parity and accessibility acceptance, then retire C/Objective-C implementations only after verified parity.

**Risks/unknowns:** Generated binding feature coverage and exact API availability need a symbol-by-symbol macOS 13 audit. Screen-coordinate conversions, display changes, Objective-C callback lifetimes, responder/key-equivalent behavior, and VoiceOver interaction require interactive macOS verification. This is a migration plan, not evidence of performance or binary-size gains; neither is guaranteed without measurement.## Findings (research checked 2026-10-14)

### Decisions

- **Toolchain:** pin Rust **1.99.0** as the initial stable toolchain, with Edition **2024** and resolver **3**. Rust 1.99.0 was released October 1, 2026; Cargo documents Edition 2024 and virtual workspace resolver configuration. This is a research recommendation, not a claim that the installed toolchain was checked. ([Rust 1.99.0 release](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2026/10/01/Rust-1.99.0/), [Cargo workspace reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/workspaces.html))

- **Platform target:** build only `aarch64-apple-darwin`, set `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=13.0`, and keep Cocoa/Metal calls behind Rust `platform/macos` interfaces. Rust supports that target from macOS 11 onward and recognizes `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET`; the repository’s stricter macOS 13 minimum remains controlling. ([Rust Apple targets](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/platform-support/apple-darwin.html), [Apple build settings](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/build-settings-reference))

- **Workspace/dependencies:** start with no third-party crates. Use a virtual root `Cargo.toml`, shared `Cargo.lock`, and `workspace.package`/`workspace.dependencies` ownership centralized with the coordinator. Suggested initial layout:
  ```

  tools/dev/
  ```
  Keep native APIs isolated; do not create unsupported-platform stubs. If Rust tooling needs JSON parsing, evaluate **serde_json = "=1.0.146"** as a narrowly scoped exception: the official tagged manifest says MIT OR Apache-2.0 and Rust 1.68 minimum; it brings serde_core, itoa, memchr, and ryu runtime dependencies. Record the tag/revision, license, transitive graph and hashes in a reviewed provenance record before adoption. ([serde_json 1.0.146 manifest](https://github.com/serde-rs/json/blob/v1.0.146/Cargo.toml); tag checked October 14, 2026.)

### Scope and ownership

CMake currently composes the app, multiple library/test/CLI targets, Cocoa/Metal frameworks, and a Python-driven `.app` bundle step. `dev` dispatches build, test, rendering, fuzz, benchmark, smoke, packaging and release workflows. Python scripts cover ledger/work-order runners, tests, corpus handling, render comparisons, perf gates, fuzzing, UI automation and packaging.

Cover these responsibilities in the eventual Rust tooling migration: `CMakeLists.txt`, `dev`, `scripts/**`, `packaging/**`, `app/test_driver/**`, and Python/shell test harnesses under `tests/**`. Preserve fixtures, schemas, artifacts and legacy source as references; port behavior and contracts without broadening platform support. Split tooling into `tools/dev` (command dispatch/build/test orchestration), `tools/ledger`, `tools/work-order`, `tools/bench`, and `tools/packaging` only as ownership boundaries become clear. Keep app and tooling crate dependencies explicit and minimal.

### Build and release tradeoffs

Use Cargo profiles as the replacement for Debug/Release configuration, with generated output in repository-local `target/`. Rust’s documented Release defaults include `opt-level=3`, no debug info, 16 codegen units, and no LTO; fewer codegen units can trade longer compile time for optimization opportunities. Benchmark candidate settings on the actual app before selecting size/performance policies. `opt-level="s"`/`"z"`, LTO, stripping and panic strategy are candidates to measure, not guaranteed binary-size wins. Do not claim Rust will be faster or smaller without measurements. ([Cargo profiles](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html), [rustc codegen options](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/codegen-options/index.html))

For controlled dependency builds, require committed lockfile and `--locked`; use offline/frozen verification only after reviewed dependency fetches. ([Cargo vendor and locked/offline behavior](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-vendor.html))

### Ready work-order sequence

1. **Rust bootstrap:** coordinator owns root manifest, lockfile, toolchain pin, Cargo config, initial `app/vexel` and `tools/dev` shells, macOS 13 target enforcement, and a no-network build/release wrapper replacing only the simplest `dev build` path. No C removal or parity claim.
2. **Build/package parity:** port app/test target graph, bundle metadata/resources/icon generation, and Debug/Release output layout.
3. **Tooling foundations:** Rust ledger/schema validation, work-order validation and runners, then Python unit-test harness contracts.
4. **Specialist tools:** corpus, golden image comparison, fuzz orchestration, benchmarks/perf gates, UI driver and packaging; separate orders with frozen interfaces and preserved evidence.
5. **Retire CMake/Python entry points** only after Rust parity gates cover each command and the owner accepts results.

### Risks and unknowns

The root Cargo manifest, crate boundaries, macOS framework bindings strategy, signing/notarization flow, and Rust equivalents for Python imaging/XML tools require specific follow-up research and ownership decisions. Dependency selection must account for MPL-2.0 project policy, transitive licenses, hashes and supply-chain review. item.text:
The earliest complete Rust desktop requires an audited Apple binding boundary, native shell, Core Text adapter, Metal presentation, and a small integration executable. Existing system wrappers do not provide AppKit integration.

Reviewed OWNER-DIRECTIVES, AGENTS, frozen native-plan and owned-document orders; named window/text/Metal headers; native shell, window events, geometry, text and presentation implementation excerpts; Rust UI/document contracts; and existing platform/toolchain research. Owned-document candidate code was not consumed.

**Proposed API contracts**

- `MainThread::acquire() -> Result<MainThread, PlatformError>` verifies Apple’s main thread. `NativeApp`, `Window`, menus, preference subscriptions, accessibility objects and presenters are `!Send + !Sync`; their operations require this capability. `NativeApp::start`, `create_window`, `run` and `shutdown` define one application lifecycle, regular activation, launch completion and autorelease pools around native turns.
- `WindowConfig` validates UTF-8, rejects embedded NUL, preserves the 1,024-byte title and 1–4,096-point dimensions. Fallible creation publishes no partially initialized handle. Public types expose no Objective-C pointers.
- `WindowId { slot, generation }` identifies callback targets. Retained native objects belong to platform owners; delegates, observers and completion blocks use invalidatable weak routing state. Callbacks enqueue owned events, never hold application-model borrows or invoke application mutation reentrantly. No Rust panic crosses Objective-C/C/block boundaries: catch unwind where supported, mark failure and request orderly shutdown; document abort behavior separately. Native exceptions must never unwind through Rust.
- `Event` separates key transitions, modifiers, committed text and composition updates. Implement `NSTextInputClient` for marked text, selection and candidate positioning; `charactersIgnoringModifiers` alone is insufficient. Translate modifier bits explicitly: C platform and accepted Rust UI constants differ.
- Preserve finite top-left point coordinates, precise scroll/magnification, monotonic timestamps and separate backing-pixel dimensions. Geometry conversion remains per-window/per-display. The accepted canvas permits integer backing scales 1–3; reject unsupported scales explicitly pending an accepted adaptation.
- Use a bounded 256-event queue with owned UTF-8/path payloads and typed overflow. Coalesce adjacent compatible motion/resize events without crossing key/button/command barriers. Reserve control capacity; saturation latches an observable fault and resets input state instead of silently losing releases or close requests. Bound native dispatch per turn; sleep/wake through the run loop.
- `FontService::layout(TextRequest) -> Result<TextLayout, TextError>` borrows inputs only during calls and returns owned metrics/outlines. Preserve 64-KiB text, 16,384 glyphs, 262,144 segments, 32 families and explicit unsupported color-glyph behavior. Main-thread-owned label rendering implements accepted `TextDraw`, retaining no text/pixel borrow; validate stride, clipping and lengths. Preserve the 64-entry/4-MiB cache bound.
- `Presenter::present(&RgbaFrame) -> Result<Submission, PresentError>` copies borrowed pixels before return. Per-window textures avoid legacy global resource coupling; bounded in-flight submissions retain GPU resources until completion. Freeze channel/alpha semantics, checked sizes and the 8,192-axis limit. Drawable absence is recoverable; readback verification stays separate.
- Menus consume command descriptors/state snapshots and emit typed commands once. AX consumes validated owned `SemanticsSnapshot`s, converts frames to screen coordinates and routes actions by window generation. Preference watching returns a removable subscription.
- Teardown invalidates routing first, cancels sheets/timers/jobs, unregisters observers and AX/menu targets, detaches delegates, retires GPU submissions, clears caches, releases windows, then stops AppKit. Late completions discard stale generations.

**Hard dependencies and proposed work orders**

1. **NATIVE-BINDINGS:** coordinator-approved dependency ADR/provenance and macOS-13 symbol audit. objc2 remains a proposal. Evaluate only required objc2/Foundation/AppKit/CoreFoundation/CoreGraphics/CoreText/Metal/QuartzCore features; justify block support separately, defer dispatch bindings. Before fetch/adoption, verify current primary manifests, exact pins, checksums, transitive licenses, SDK-derived provenance, compiler compatibility and callback APIs. Existing research establishes neither newest versions nor verified licenses.
2. **NATIVE-SHELL:** map `platform_window*.m`, native-shell/internal headers and geometry into startup, windows, responder/input, queues and teardown.
3. **NATIVE-TEXT-PRESENT:** map both text implementations and Metal/shaders into font/draw/presenter contracts.
4. **NATIVE-MENU-AX:** map menu and accessibility implementations, command routing and preferences.
5. **DESKTOP-CHECKPOINT:** bundle executable/resources; connect accepted custom UI to these seams. First usable GUI: labeled interactive custom canvas, keyboard/IME, resize/scale, menus, VoiceOver and clean close.

Document opening additionally requires accepted owned-document APIs: immutable `Arc<Vec<u8>>`, offset spans, cancellation and generation-tagged bounded job results. No self-referential borrowed model.

MacOS-26 material branches require availability guards; macOS-13 compatibility remains unverified. All first-party implementation stays Rust behind platform interfaces: custom UI, owned SVG, no C shims, GPL source or unsupported-OS backends.

No edits, network, downloads, installs, builds, tests, agents or commits occurred. This is an architecture proposal, with no product-completion or performance claim.
